Too many third and longs, too many second and longs. “I think for us, one of the huge focuses is how do we get the run game back and what do we got to do to get the ball in the right people’s hands.” Alabama freshman Trae’shawn Brown started at running back, running 11 times for 35 yards. Daniel Hill added 15 yards on five carries, while Kevin Riley was the only other running back to receive a snap, playing one. Sophomore AK Dear and freshman EJ Crowell were both listed as questionable on the availability report during the week before being upgraded and cleared to play Saturday. Both were in uniform for pregame warmups, with Crowell wearing a brace over his left knee, but neither played in the game. “They got to get healthy,” Grubb said. “They got to get healthy. It sucks. I’d love to give EJ the ball 32 times a game, but we just got to get him healthy, man. My heart breaks for both those kids because they’re tough as nails. They’ve got to go through it. They work their asses off every week to get back on the field, and we’re hoping. We hope every week. “I know, again, those guys are working so hard to get back out there. They’ve done a good job with staying on the preparation, doing their homework, doing the walk throughs, doing everything they’re supposed to do. EJ tried to give it a go before the game, and had the brace on, and just really wasn’t capable of doing that. We’re hopeful and obviously we’re lucky they’re not season-ending injuries or anything like that, and they’re just working to get healthy.” Grubb gave us plenty of good quotables this week, but the part that got the most time in airwaves was his talking about the run game. For my part, I have no issues with the way Grubb called this game (and I’ve had plenty of issues with Grubb in the past). I liked how they approached the gameplan to keep things conservative early, then as Keelon Russell seemed to get more settled in, he leaned further into the pass to go and get that lead. I’d like to see more success rushing, of course, but even though the yards weren’t great, they also avoided negative rushing plays. And 3rd and 4 is sooooo much better than 3rd and 11. Next, Kane Wommack gave us a 15-minute presser this time around, if you’re so inclined. Wommack talked some about this being a massive shift in schematic approach between the LSU and the Vanderbilt offense, so I’m interested to see how he approaches that. It sounds like that Vandy game in 2024 still bothers him more than about anything else from his tenure. “That game obviously had a major impact on me,” Wommack said. Alabama’s previous trip to Vanderbilt came one week after beating Georgia and climbing to No. 1 in the country. The unranked Commodores handed the Crimson Tide a shocking 40-35 loss, their first victory in the series since 1984. Wommack says what went wrong started with an urgency Alabama failed to carry into the matchup. “We came off of a big win. I think we went up there two years ago, and we didn’t have enough guys on the sideline that had the same sense of urgency that you have to have in every single SEC game,” Wommack said. He said the block serves as a reminder of how relentless Alabama must remain in its preparation. The staff has drawn from that experience numerous times since the loss, using it to reinforce the standard required to win games in conference play. Now Alabama has another significant road victory behind and another week to show it can reset. Next up, Kalen DeBoer: DeBoer on Zabien Brown, William Sanders’ statuses… “Zabien has got the lower-extremity injury. Got some snaps, and I think any snaps that we could get out of him on the weekend was gonna be a positive. Obviously, he’s on the football field, first of all, and I think that’s impactful. His presence, and then I think also, just the number of snaps that took off some of the other guys. So, I think he’s coming along, day-to-day. He played last week, and really didn’t feel like there was a setback. It was just gonna be limited on what he could give us. He pushed it as far as we felt he could push himself. So, getting him back this week is something I would expect. Just keep progressing. “And then William Sanders, we feel good about his progress. It’s been a quick turnaround for him. Realistically, knew that it would be really hard to get him on the football field. Went through warmups, and then we knew he wouldn’t be a starter, but we were trying to figure out if in an emergency role, if that could happen. So, we’ll keep progressing, but we need some improvements this week to get to where he can go out there and be competitive to the level we need him.” DeBoer on balancing Keelon Russell’s health vs. progress… “We gotta keep moving and winning and playing our best football. So, you’re weighing how he feels, what the medical staff says as far as — we never want to hurt him, and we will never do that. But he’s gotta go out there and obviously be able to play at the level that can help us win. So, we got a lot of confidence if we had to move to Austin [Mack] at some point. But he’s day-to-day. I mean, he continued to finish off the game. And so, that’s a good sign right there. I mean, this kid’s a really tough kid. “And he’s had other things that have popped up in games where he’s played through it. You guys have seen probably that, too, when you’re really paying close attention. And he stays out on the football field, keeps doing his thing. So, for him to play at the level he played at, getting dinged up a little bit, is impressive in itself. I’d expect him to do everything he can to get on the football field. And we’re never gonna put him in an area of safety where that’s a concern.” Continuing to play without Zabien Brown has been one of the least-talked about aspects of Alabama’s team this season. He’s one of the best corners in the country, and without him, the defensive scheme has shifted to pushing their corners further and further back the last few weeks. Seriously, think about where Alabama was during the Tennessee game: They were missing Zabien Brown and Ryan Coleman-Williams – both team captains, both All-Americans, and both considered the Tide’s top two NFL draft picks. They were also missing Terrance Green and Racin Delgatty, the two players most central on the line of scrimmage on every play. It’s been a tough stretch for the Tide, and I think it hasn’t gotten enough media attention as they’ve had some midseason struggles. We’ll be previewing Vandy more later this week, but it looks like Clark Lea is tinkering with their roster a bit ahead of the Bama game. NASHVILLE-Vanderbilt has made a number of notable moves on its depth chart prior to its Tuesday matchup with Alabama. Highly-regarded freshman offensive lineman Mitchell Smith is listed as Vanderbilt’s starter at strong guard and former Vanderbilt safety Dontae Carter is now listed at cornerback-as the

item.title: Ricky Stenhouse Jr. Draws Hard Line Between His Past And Hocevar’s Drama
item.description: Vasha Hunt-Imagn Images Ricky Stenhouse Jr. knows exactly what it costs to lose a ride for crashing. He sat out races early in his career after the team grew tired of his mistakes. Now he watches Carson Hocevar face a much harsher fate for a very different reason. Stenhouse admits his own past was messy, but he insists Hocevar crossed a line that he never did. The veteran driver spoke to reporter Tim Moore ahead of the Homestead-Miami finale. He laughed when asked about the parallel between his benching and the rookie’s suspension. Stenhouse made it clear that his past actions were just bad driving, while Hocevar’s moves were pure revenge. “I did it, you know; the reason I set out is because I was pushing the car harder than it could go and making mistakes,” Stenhouse Jr. said, according to Yahoo Sports . “I wasn’t intentionally spinning out or wrecking people. So I think it’s totally different,” he added. A Clear Line in the Paint The difference comes down to intent. Stenhouse crashed because he was a rookie trying to go faster than his car could handle. Jack Roush’s team sat him out to teach him a lesson about control. They stopped him after he wrecked five of his first twelve races and destroyed two cars in one weekend. That was a cost of doing business for a young driver learning the ropes. Hocevar’s situation involves a deliberate attack. He brake-checked Austin Cindric on purpose at Martinsville, applying over 1,000 pounds of pressure to cause a crash. Cindric finished 36th and dropped three spots in the standings because of the hit. For conduct harmful to stock car racing, NASCAR imposed a $100,000 fine on Hocevar and removed 25 points from his total. The team also made the call to bench him for the season finale. Spire Motorsports replaced him with Justin Haley. This was not a mistake born of inexperience. It was a calculated move to hurt a rival in a tight title race. Stenhouse sees the gap between his errors and Hocevar’s malice. Other Drivers Weigh In Not everyone is waiting for an explanation. Zane Smith has been fighting with Hocevar for months. Smith called him a “goon” back in July after they crashed at Chicagoland and Nashville. He was fined $50,000 himself for ramming Hocevar after the Phoenix race. Now that Hocevar is out of the finale, Smith has no sympathy. Smith’s history with the No. 77 driver includes a crash at Iowa in 2025 and another at Chicagoland in July 2026. He felt Hocevar acted like nothing happened after apologizing on track, only to act differently on social media. The rivalry has heated up since NASCAR warned both drivers at Atlanta. The Phoenix incident proved the warning was ignored. Smith knows the cost of this feud, but he does not see Hocevar’s suspension as a tragedy. The Focus Shifts to the Finish Austin Cindric remains focused on the points battle despite the chaos. item.title: ‘Take the blame’ – Former NBA champion calls Doc Rivers ‘weird’ for Giannis Antetokounmpo comments
item.description: Photo by Tim Nwachukwu/Getty Images Doc Rivers’ seemingly critical comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo have created massive discourse, and one former Laker has taken exception to what he said. It is very rare that people within the NBA fraternity speak negatively about one another to the media. Whatever the issues are behind the scenes, they tend not to come out. So when Doc Rivers was recently critical of his former superstar, Giannis Antetokounmpo, the situation blew up quickly. Rivers made comments about the difficulty of coaching the Greek Freak and seemingly called out his playing style. Antetokounmpo was visibly shocked when told of the comments, calling them ‘insane’. Doc has since reportedly apologised, but fans and the media alike have a lot to say about the issue. Metta Sandiford-Artest asks coaches to stop blaming players after Doc Rivers’ comments The relationship between players and coaches in the NBA can be tenuous at times. It is rarely worse than when a team with expectations fails to deliver, like the Milwaukee Bucks did during Rivers’ tenure. There is plenty of blame to go around in those situations, and nobody really wants it. Regardless, for Rivers to suggest openly that Giannis is difficult to coach is something a lot of people have taken issue with. And former NBA champion Metta Sandiford-Artest has vocalised the issue. “Weird that a person would throw Giannis Antetokounmpo under the bus,” Sandiford-Artest wrote in a post on X. “Makes no sense. All he does is work hard and (bring) championships to the Milwaukee. Coach Metta so ready to take the blame. Coaches, stop blaming players.” The former Laker currently works as a coach in women’s college basketball, which may explain why he is weighing in on the matter. Rivers himself has clarified his comments since he made them, but that doesn’t mean that everyone in the basketball world will let them slide. Read more: ‘Life is short’ – Stephen A. item.title: Tuesday Cannon Fodder: sacked?
item.description: MANCHESTER, ENGLAND - NOVEMBER 08: Michael Carrick, head coach / manager of Manchester United reacts during the Premier League 2026/27 match between Manchester United and Aston Villa FC at Old Trafford on November 08, 2026 in Manchester, England. (Photo by Catherine Ivill - AMA/Getty Images) | Getty Images Good Tuesday morning, TSFers! I read that 20 of Arsenal’s 25 first team players are out on international duty. Noni Madueke was a weird omission from the England lineup. Bukayo Saka and William Saliba aren’t fit. So that’s the two backup keepers then. My goodness. This squad is insanely deep and talented. The news of the day (yesterday) was that Manchester United plan to sack Michael Carrick. Sure, whatever. You do you, fam. I don’t think that Carrick is the problem at that club. The move will likely improve the team because the players had quit on him and the situation had become untenable. If you’re the next manager, how could you have any confidence that the leadership core of that roster won’t quit on you if they wake up on the wrong side of the bed? My opinion: Manchester United’s players are nowhere near good enough to do what is expected of Manchester United players, i.e. compete for trophies. They haven’t been for a while. Giving Bruno Fernandes the Premier League POTY award was a joke. For the few of you who were curious, I intended to sit the Vikings defense but forgot. Better to be lucky than good, they scored a handful of points anyway. That Vikings offense is bad , which is a shame because their defense is really good. Staying in NFL-land: the Jaguars are going for it, eh? Will this be the Bills’ year? Or will someone like the Bears win the Super Bowl because the AFC beats the tar out of each other in the playoffs and softens up whoever wins that conference?

item.title: John Harbaugh, Giants Given ‘Trust’ Warning About Trade Plans
item.description: John Harbaugh and the New York Giants have been given a warning about "trade trust" before the deadline. Getty John Harbaugh sounds increasingly open to adding fresh talent before the 2026 NFL trade deadline at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, November 10, but his best-laid plans could be undone if the New York Giants don’t heed a warning about losing “trust” with potential trade partners around the league. The note of caution is sounded by “NFL Blue Book” Substack writer and All-Pro voter Charles Robinson. He pointed out how the Giants and Harbaugh “have now exposed *two* failed behind-the-curtain trade pursuits inside 1 week, between their Simmons and Taylor efforts. Whether fans like it or not (or reporters), this is the kind of thing that turns future trade partners off. Expose failed deals, lose trade trust.” #Giants have now exposed *two* failed behind-the-curtain trade pursuits inside 1 week, between their Simmons and Taylor efforts. Whether fans like it or not (or reporters), this is the kind of thing that turns future trade partners off. Expose failed deals, lose trade trust. 💯% https://t.co/G62C1azPvb — Charles Robinson (@CharlesRobinson) November 9, 2026 It’s a valid concern after it became public the Giants took a two-draft pick trade package for Indianapolis Colts’ running back Jonathan Taylor off the table. This news was on the heels of Harbaugh freely admitting to going around Tennessee Titans’ general manager Mike Borgonzi to try and swing a deal for All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . The way the Giants approached a potential deal for Simmons, by going directly to owner Amy Adams Strunk, raised the concerns about trust Robinson cited. Those concerns could prove damaging on a day when Harbaugh remains blunt about adding to his playoff-chasing team. He’s still searching for reinforcements at two key spots. John Harbaugh’s Risking ‘Trust’ With Brazen Trade Strategy The reason the Giants couldn’t land Simmons ahead of the Chicago Bears “really came down to trust,” according to Robinson . He noted how “the Titans were trying to keep talks regarding Simmons as quiet as possible.” Robinson doesn’t “think the Titans trusted the Giants to keep the talks private. I think Tennessee believed that any unsuccessful talks with the Giants would have been leaked. And frankly, given what has unfolded since the trade went down, I think the Titans were right.” Keeping things private so those involved in a trade can save face, even when talks go nowhere, creates goodwill between teams. Especially when talks go nowhere. The Giants have been reckless with this goodwill twice, but Harbaugh isn’t wavering in his direct approach. Instead, the Super Bowl-winning former head coach of the Baltimore Ravens remains committed to not waiting to improve the Giants’ roster. Harbaugh told reporters on Monday, November 9, “The now weighs more important than the future, if you’re gonna put it on a scale. And you go from there,” per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News

And you go from there,” per Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News , who concluded, “Yeah. The Giants will be adding a player, or players.” John Harbaugh on the NFL trade deadline: "The now weighs more important than the future, if you're gonna put it on a scale. And you go from there." Yeah. The Giants will be adding a player, or players — Pat Leonard (@PLeonardNYDN) November 9, 2026 Those players are already known after Harbaugh’s assessment of the obvious weak spots on this Giants team. Giants Have Obvious Needs to Fix Before Deadline Harbaugh would like a marquee lead running back, but that might be wishful thinking. His more realistic option involves beefing up the interior of the defensive line. The Giants are wisely pivoting in this direction . What they’re seeing is a trade market brimming with sturdy and capable defensive tackles. That market includes a dominant and bargain run-stuffer who’d help veteran nose guard D.J. Reader’ s efforts to fix a longstanding weakness . There’s also the possibility of the Giants adding an experienced and popular Super Bowl champion to the heart of their evolving defensive front. Both of these would-be deals appear easier to engineer than any move for help in the backfield. Even trying to add a supporting runner has proved difficult for Harbaugh, but recruiting a new D-tackle should be more straightforward. The only thing that could scupper the plan is if the Giants have lost more trust than they expected after their public pursuits of Simmons and Taylor. item.title: “Extremely Unprofessional Behavior” – Tennis Fans Furious After ‘Awful’ Comment On Aryna Sabalenka from Unnamed Broadcaster At WTA Finals
item.description: Aug 8, 2026; Toronto, Ontario, Canada; Aryna Sabalenka reacts after missing a point against Ekaterina Alexandrova (not pictured) during the fourth round at the National Bank Open at Sobeys Stadium. © John E. Sokolowski-Imagn Images Tennis fans expressed their dissent at a broadcaster’s disrespectful remark about Aryna Sabalenka’s look during the 2026 WTA Finals. Sabalenka, Coco Gauff, Jessica Pegula, Elena Rybakina, and other WTA stars showed off their looks for the 2026 WTA Finals photoshoot on media day. The Belarusian tennis player wore a red top and jacket paired with a black leather skirt. She completed her look with a stack of jewelry, red socks, and black pointed stilettos. During the photoshoot, one commentator’s mic was left on, and the commentator was heard making an offensive comment. “Look, look… she looks awful,” the commentator said. The demeaning comment did not sit well with fans; one of them called it disgraceful and unprofessional and demanded strict action. “This sounds like disgraceful and extremely unprofessional behavior from one of your commentators @florenthouzot. I hope they will be punished, and I hope Sabalenka will not do any more interviews with this broadcaster again,” the fan wrote. A fan criticized the broadcaster for making the disrespectful comment and demanded a ban. “Criticizing a woman. They should identify him and ban him from tennis courts for 🤡🤡. The state of sports journalism is just going downhill every day.” Another fan simply wrote: Here are a few more reactions: “HAHAHAHA But what’s going on with the open mics at this tournament? At this point it seems like they’re doing it on purpose, to stir up drama like a soap opera,” a fan wrote. “What do you mean, horrible? She’s a beautiful woman. He must be an envious 🦆,” another fan added. “I hope they identify him, and that he never gets to set foot on a tennis court again, the ‘sports journalism’ that’s been so awful lately,” one fan chimed in. Aryna Sabalenka makes her feelings known about facing Karolina Muchova ahead of the WTA Finals run Aryna Sabalenka played her sixth consecutive WTA Finals in 2026. In her match, she fought back from a break down in both sets to win 7-6(7-2), 7-5 against Karolina Muchova. She landed 59% of her first serves and won 33 of 44 points behind them. Before facing Muchova, Sabalenka praised the Czech player’s talent and versatility, saying she has a strong serve, powerful shots, good movement, and excellent net play. Sabalenka further added that she enjoys playing against her (via Tennis World USA). “She’s [an] amazing player. She really has variety in the game, approaches the net, great touch. We had a lot of great, tough battles, close matches. She’s very challenging, moving well, with heavy strokes, great serving, and an aggressive net game. She’s a tricky player to face. I always enjoy playing against her.” Aryna Sabalenka will face French Open champion Mirra Andreeva in the next group match at the WTA Finals. Read more at

item.title: ‘Changes The Lakers’ Upside’ — NBA Insider Pushes LAL To Abandon Center Search, Swing Move For Luka Dončić’s $88M Ex-Teammate
item.description: ‘Changes The Lakers’ Upside’ — NBA Insider Pushes LAL To Abandon Center Search, Swing Move For Luka Dončić’s $88M Ex-Teammate The Los Angeles Lakers have won 10 of their first 12 games and sit first in the Western Conference. That start has not stopped talk about what the Lakers could add before the trade deadline. In a show clip posted Monday, Lakers analyst Jovan Buha made the case that landing Dallas Mavericks forward P.J. Washington, Luka Dončić’s former teammate, would do more for the Lakers than adding a backup center. Jovan Buha Explains Why a Forward Comes Before a Backup Center Buha described the kind of player he has in mind and measured Washington against Herb, an apparent reference to New Orleans Pelicans forward Herbert Jones. “I just think PJ, for what the Lakers specifically need, we’re talking about a bigger wing, a guy who can battle in the paint, a guy who could battle on the glass, a guy who can also space the floor and be an off-ball threat. That’s way more PJ than it is Herb.” He then weighed that move against help at center. “PJ, to me, it’s like that’s the thing that changes the Lakers’ upside, in my opinion, more than even the backup five. Like, I think if there’s a way to get a good starting forward, I would take that even ahead of a good backup five, because I think that locks in the starters, the closers. And I think it just gives them a higher upside.” He also compared two centers, apparently Pelicans center Yves Missi and Mavericks center Moussa Cissé. “I do like Cissé, but I do like Missi far more,” Buha said. READ MORE: ‘Never Got a Chance,’ ‘Such a Big Jump’ – 3-Time NBA All-Star Makes Case for Lakers Star Austin Reaves’ Readiness To Be a No. 1 Option Buha did not say the Lakers should stop looking for a center, and in the clip he offered the idea as his own view, not as word of any talks between the teams. Washington already has a history with Dončić. Dallas acquired him from the Charlotte Hornets before the 2024 trade deadline, and he played alongside Dončić on the Mavericks team that reached the NBA Finals four months later. Washington is a 6-foot-6 forward. In 2024-25, the season before he signed his extension, he averaged 14.7 points, a career-high 7.8 rebounds and 2.3 assists while shooting 45.3% from the field and 38.1% from the 3-point range. He started Monday’s 125-122 win over the Indiana Pacers and had 13 points on 4-of-12 shooting, including 2 of 8 from 3, with nine rebounds, two steals and two blocks in 35 minutes. Any trade would also mean taking on a long contract. Washington’s agency, LIFT Sports Management, confirmed the agreement in September 2025, and the Mavericks announced the extension that month without releasing its terms. The Associated Press, citing a person with knowledge of the extension, put it at four years and $89 million. READ MORE: ‘How Dare You? I Bought My Tickets This Close So I Can Do That’ — 3-Time All-Star Defends Pistons Heckler Who Went After Lakers’ Bronny James The extensi

item.title: FIA president confirms F1 season will end in Qatar and Abu Dhabi
item.description: FILE PHOTO - British Formula One driver Lewis Hamilton of team Ferrari leads team mate Charles Leclerc at the start of the Mexican Grand Prix at the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. (is associated with: «FIA president confirms F1 season will end in Qatar and Abu Dhabi») Bradley Collyer/PA Wire/dpa FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem has confirmed the Formula One season will finish with the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix as planned. Earlier in the year, both the races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were postponed because of safety concerns in the region in the wake of the Iran war. "We are ready for Qatar and Abu Dhabi," Ben Sulayem said in a post on Instagram. "We are fully prepared and committed to delivering two outstanding Grands Prix weekends and a spectacular conclusion to the FIA Formula One World Championship. "We are working closely with our partners to ensure everything is in place for our drivers, teams and fans. We look forward to welcoming everyone for two thrilling weekends of racing and an unforgettable finish to the Formula One season."

item.title: The strange reason Japan can’t pick their best fly half against England
item.description: In the aftermath of his side’s defeat to Wales, the Japan head coach Eddie Jones already had more than half an eye on England . “We’ll need to be able to break up the game,” the veteran schemer said with a glint in his eye and a familiar smirk on his face. “If we play an orthodox game of rugby, we’re probably going to struggle to beat them. And the English don’t react well to unorthodox rugby. We’ve got to think about how we can play quite unorthodoxly.” Jones speaks, of course, from experience. It was his England side that were baffled by Italy’s radical ruck tactics in the Six Nations in 2017 ; in a neat twist, Conor O’Shea, the architect of that plan, now heads up performance at England’s Rugby Football Union (RFU). “Maybe we’ll play like Italy did in 2017,” Jones teased. “Can you still play like that in the rucks? I don’t think you can, can you?” Eddie Jones has promised to throw a few curveballs at England (Getty) England are bracing for something similarly avant-garde nonetheless. It is instructive, though, that Jones is having to talk in such terms about a side he does not yet see as an equal to the world’s top teams. Japan beat Italy and pushed Ireland close in July, before coming within three points of Australia in August – they have the talent to at least give England a fright. There is one key difference from those games, though. In each of those encounters, Japan were steered from fly half by Ryunosuke Ito, a 21-year-old playmaker long tipped for a bright future who was named to start against France before he had even played a senior club game. He took to Test rugby like a natural; through the Nations Championship, Australia series and Pacific Nations Cup, the No 10 shirt was his. For a team that had struggled to replace Yu Tamura, and with Lee Seung Sin injured, here was the welcome emergence of a new, young star. Ryunosuke Ito has emerged as a budding star for Japan (Getty) That flourishing has been brought to a strange and unwelcome halt, though. Ito is not in the United Kingdom with the rest of Jones’s squad, with Riku Kitahara steering the ship against Wales in Cardiff instead. Kitahara performed well; about as well as one might expect of a player reportedly described by Jones as his fourth-choice fly half. There is no injury to speak of to Ito. Why, then, is he absent? Well, it has to do with a strange rugby hierarchy that persists in Japan. While his colleagues are battling the best in men’s Test rugby in Europe, Ito will be obliged to pull on the shirt of Meiji University as he completes his education. “He’s the only 10 for a tier one nation in the world who has to go and play for an amateur team now,” Jones complained after the recent defeat to Fiji, according to rugbyjp.com . “Imagine if [baseball superstar] Shohei Ohtani went back to play for Keio University.” It is a challenge that just about every homegrown Japan international faces. item.content:encoded: In the aftermath of his side’s defeat to Wales, the Japan head coach Eddie Jones already had more than half an eye on England . “We’ll need to be able to break up the game,” the veteran schemer said with a glint in his eye and a familiar smirk on his face. “If we play an orthodox game of rugby, we’re probably going to struggle to beat them. And the English don’t react well to unorthodox rugby. We’ve got to think about how we can play quite unorthodoxly.” Jones speaks, of course, from experience. It was his England side that were baffled by Italy’s radical ruck tactics in the Six Nations in 2017 ; in a neat twist, Conor O’Shea, the architect of that plan, now heads up performance at England’s Rugby Football Union (RFU). “Maybe we’ll play like Italy did in 2017,” Jones teased. “Can you still play like that in the rucks? I don’t think you can, can you?” Eddie Jones has promised to throw a few curveballs at England (Getty) England are bracing for something similarly avant-garde nonetheless. It is instructive, though, that Jones is having to talk in such terms about a side he does not yet see as an equal to the world’s top teams. Japan beat Italy and pushed Ireland close in July, before coming within three points of Australia in August – they have the talent to at least give England a fright. There is one key difference from those games, though. In each of those encounters, Japan were steered from fly half by Ryunosuke Ito, a 21-year-old playmaker long tipped for a bright future who was named to start against France before he had even played a senior club game. He took to Test rugby like a natural; through the Nations Championship, Australia series and Pacific Nations Cup, the No 10 shirt was his. For a team that had struggled to replace Yu Tamura, and with Lee Seung Sin injured, here was the welcome emergence of a new, young star. Ryunosuke Ito has emerged as a budding star for Japan (Getty) That flourishing has been brought to a strange and unwelcome halt, though. Ito is not in the United Kingdom with the rest of Jones’s squad, with Riku Kitahara steering the ship against Wales in Cardiff instead. Kitahara performed well; about as well as one might expect of a player reportedly described by Jones as his fourth-choice fly half. There is no injury to speak of to Ito. Why, then, is he absent? Well, it has to do with a strange rugby hierarchy that persists in Japan. While his colleagues are battling the best in men’s Test rugby in Europe, Ito will be obliged to pull on the shirt of Meiji University as he completes his education. “He’s the only 10 for a tier one nation in the world who has to go and play for an amateur team now,” Jones complained after the recent defeat to Fiji, according to rugbyjp.com . “Imagine if [baseball superstar] Shohei Ohtani went back to play for Keio University.” It is a challenge that just about every homegrown Japan international faces. The development pathway is clear in the country, with young players on average making their senior club debut about three years later than those in England, for example. As a model, it is more akin to that of the NFL, and can bring benefits in preparing individuals for life after rugby – take the former wing Kenki Fukuoka, who burned brightly in a six-year international career before retiring at the age of 28 to become a doctor. The former Japan wing Kenki Fukuoka retired early from rugby to become a doctor (Getty) Of course, Jones would rather have Ito as his disposal, but some time off may be no bad thing for a player adjusting to the highest level. These are fascinating times more generally for Japanese rugby, too. Changes to the eligibility of international players within the Japan Rugby League One are set to be introduced for the next campaign, which may limit opportunities for overseas players and – more controversially – naturalised citizens. That may in part explain the raft of Springboks announced to be returning to South Africa in recent weeks, although other factors are at play. Homegrown player development remains an area of emphasis for Japan. A look at their squad that faced Wales was evidence of how they have used their international imports well, getting the best out of one another. Dylan Riley – born in South Africa, schooled in Australia – has emerged as an excellent centres since joining the Saitama Wild Knights in 2018, while the second row partnership of Warner Dearns and Harry Hockings is as imposing as any in the world, making up for an historic shortcoming. Warner Dearns (right) and Harry Hockings have added heft and leadership to the Japan pack (Getty) Wellington-born Dearns was arguably the best lock in Super Rugby Pacific during a title-winning campaign with the Hurricanes – and rebuffed an approach from the All Blacks to switch allegiance, noting all that Japan had given him. "I turned them down and said I'd come back and play [in Japan],” the outstanding second row explained. “I went to high school in Japan, was invited into the national team training camp, and was given so many opportunities. It would be a waste to throw all of that away and go and play for New Zealand." An imperfect system it may be but Japan are prepared to do things differently.

item.title: Germany's AfD and The Left in favour of Russia at ice hockey worlds
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Fans wave German flags during the Deutschland Cup Ice Hockey match between Germany and Slovakia at the PSD Bank Dome. (is associated with: «Germany's AfD and The Left in favour of Russia at ice hockey worlds») Markus Lenhardt/dpa German far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party and The Left have spoken in favour of the participation of Russia in the 2027 men's ice hockey championships in Germany. "We consider this a return to normality. Of course, visas should also be granted to the Russian athletes," Jörn König, the AfD parliamentary group's sports policy spokesman, told the news portal ZDFheute.de. König, who has condemned the Moscow's war in Ukraine, also pointed out that the United States are never excluded from international competition, even though the nation has waged "wars in violation of international law." The International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) opted to continue to exclude Russian teams from competition on security grounds. But Russia appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which ruled in the country's favour. The backlash against the CAS decision has spread through sport, politics and business. The Left believes the CAS ruling should be accepted. "We must no longer ignore this regrettable reality," said Christian Görke, the party's spokesman on sports policy. He pointed out that Russian athletes are now competing again in other sports. A spokesperson for State Minister for Sport Ronald Rauhe told ZDFheute.de that Russia's participation would make hosting the world championships "virtually impossible for sporting and economic reasons." Germany initially threatened to give back the hosting rights for the tournament, but the country's ice hockey boss said on Sunday this is no longer an option. "We want to hold the world championship in Germany next year, and I am also very optimistic that we will manage that," German Ice Hockey Federation (DEB) chief executive Frank Lutz told reporters. However, participating nations, such as world champions Finland, have threatened to boycott the tournament in case Russia is allowed to participate. Media reports say Russia is being persuaded to pull out after nations and also sponsors threatened a boycott.

item.title: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez is quietly having a Pro Bowl year
item.description: The Cleveland Browns are having a roller coaster of a season. They have beaten only one good team , the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 4, defeated four other clubs considered mediocre, and lost to two bad teams . And now they are faced with some difficult games on their schedule, namely playing their division foe, the Cincinnati Bengals, twice. RELATED: BOJORQUEZ INTERVIEW Consider the fact that there aren’t any really good teams left on their schedule. Could they still make the playoffs? A division title seems out of reach, but it takes 10 or 11 wins to get that #7 seed, and they are already halfway to that goal. There are several players on the Browns roster who are having a good year. Guys like TE Harold Fannin, LBs Carson Schwesinger and Quincy Williams, plus DT Mason Graham are getting their fair share of press regarding possibly getting some major Pro Bowl votes. But one player stands out, and nobody is talking about his season: Browns punter Corey Bojorquez. The Boot is back 🥾 We've re-signed P Corey Bojorquez! 📰 Read more: https://t.co/wQ4NPLBAHA pic.twitter.com/r7RsK8WdCa — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) March 12, 2026 Guys who make their living on special teams are usually only noticed when they miss a field goal, or both a punt, or skip a pass to the holder. Bojo has quietly been killing it as Cleveland’s punter this season. He was re-signed during last March’s free agency period. Currently, he is listed #5 in the league in net average per punt with 44.0 yards. The league leader is just 46.1, so Bojorquez is keeping the rankings tight. He is ranked #4 in average distance per kick at 50.4. Again, the leader’s number is close at 51.8, so one game could alter these numbers. Usually, the punters with the most kicks in a season are on teams whose offensive units can’t finish drives, or are unable to sustain drives. Bojo is ranked #3 in the most punts with 43. The league leader plays for the Philadelphia Eagles, which backs up this stat goes to guys who are on struggling offensive teams. He booted a season-high eight punts in the loss to the New York Jets when the offense could not move the ball. Bojo is considered a field flipper . This means his kicks can alter the opposing team’s field position just off one punt that has traveled 50+ yards. Case in point, in Week 3 against the Carolina Panthers, Bojorquez’s first punt was for 68 yards. Pretty good, eh? His first punt of the second half was 60 yards. Then his final kick was for a whopping 81 yards that went from Cleveland’s 19-yard line into the end zone. The NFL record for the longest punt is Steve O’Neal’s 98-yarder in 1969 while playing for the New York Jets: Take a look at Bojorquez’s 2026 season stats: Week 1 Punts: 3 Yards: 130 Yards per punt average: 43.3 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 48 yards Week 2 Punts: 4 Yards: 198 Yards per punt average: 49.5 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 2 Blocked: 0 Long: 57 yards Week 3 Punts: 5

The NFL record for the longest punt is Steve O’Neal’s 98-yarder in 1969 while playing for the New York Jets: Take a look at Bojorquez’s 2026 season stats: Week 1 Punts: 3 Yards: 130 Yards per punt average: 43.3 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 48 yards Week 2 Punts: 4 Yards: 198 Yards per punt average: 49.5 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 2 Blocked: 0 Long: 57 yards Week 3 Punts: 5 Yards: 243 Yards per punt average: 48.6 Net yards per punt average: 45.8 Downed inside the 20: 3 Blocked: 0 Long: 62 yards Week 4 Punts: 4 Yards: 251 Yards per punt average: 62.8 Net yards per punt average: 50.3 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 81 yards Week 5 Punts: 8 Yards: 421 Yards per punt average: 52.6 Net yards per punt average: 41.8 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 67 yards Week 6 Punts: 7 Yards: 315 Yards per punt average: 48.0 Net yards per punt average: 36.7 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 62 yards Week 7 Punts: 3 Yards: 144 Yards per punt average: 48.0 Net yards per punt average: 45.0 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 59 yards Week 8 Punts: 4 Yards: 199 Yards per punt average: 49.8 Net yards per punt average: 49.8 Downed inside the 20: 3 Blocked: 0 Long: 58 yards Week 9 Punts: 5 Yards: 267 Yards per punt average: 53.4 Net yards per punt average: 39.8 Downed inside the 20: 1 Blocked: 0 Long: 59 yards When a running back breaks a play for 15 yards, those numbers are added to his game rushing stats. But with a punter, he could boot one for 56 yards, and then have it returned for 25 yards, which affects his net average; in this case, that stat would be 31.0 yards. Whereas a fair catch or a touchback gives the punter the exact distance of the kick. So, something the punter has zero control over can affect his overall stats. What is not considered is what kind of 56-yarder this is. Let’s say that this punt has a hangtime of 3.91 seconds and comes down in the center of the field. Even factoring in a long operation time, can one of the gunners get to the spot where the ball finally descends? Even if the gunner had nobody blocking him, there wouldn’t be a chance of this happening because that gunner would need to travel nearly 60 yards in just over 6 seconds. The punt is going to be returned. Another obstacle on a punt is if the returner doesn’t catch the ball and lets it hit the turf. We all know that because of the shape of a football, it can go almost anywhere. Including backwards. This could take off as much as 10 yards on a punt before it is downed. Yet another obstacle to getting larger numbers for punters is the pooch kick. This usually happens when the offense stalls out within 10 yards of the midfield stripe. A long field goal attempt is considered, but the coach decides it is out of the question. And the coach doesn’t want to go for it, whether that is because of field position or an unreasonable down-and-distance. So, the punter trots out. Now, there isn’t much advantage to boom the kick for a touchback, so the kicker wants the ball to land inside the 10-yard line, preferably. And if he accomplishes this, the kick itself may have been downed at the three-yard line, but the punt only traveled less than 40 yards. That is a huge plus for flipping field position for the team, but it hurts the punter’s average. The only positive stat is the “inside the 20” tabulation. But that is pretty vague in itself. There should be another stat that says “inside the 5” to distinguish punters who have the ability to make the ball travel higher so that it descends closer to the goal line. For the past eight games, Bojorquez has had at least one kick of 58 yards or longer. He routinely has contests where he has multiple punts in the 50+ range. That becomes a weapon. His talents were on full display in the loss to the New Orleans Saints . The Browns had to punt after their first possession. Bojo punted from Cleveland’s 26-yard line and was downed at the Saints’ 26. Their next possession was also a punt that went from the Browns’ 40-yard line to New Orleans’ 14-yard line. That’s flipping the field. ball back baby!!!!! #CLEvsNO on CBS pic.twitter.com/JJcPTOYU9p — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) November 8, 2026 Bojo’s only punt in Quarter 2 went to the 20-yard line, where Saints returner Barion Brown fumbled, and Cleveland safety Donovan McMillan recovered. But the kick had traveled 57 yards first. His fourth punt also went 57 yards, while his final punt in the fourth quarter traveled 59 yards from Cleveland’s 16-yard line to the Saints’ 25. This is Bojorquez’s ninth year in the league. In 202, he led the league in yards per punt average with 50.8 while with the Buffalo Bills, kicking about a third of his punts in freezing weather. In 2024, he led the league in number of punts (89) and total yardage (4,387). Last year, Bojo led the league in the same two categories, kicking 91 total punts and gaining 4,165 yards. In three different years, he had the longest recorded punt: 2020 – 72 yards, 2021 – 82 yards, and 2024 – 84 yards. He is also leading this year with that 81-yarder in the Steelers game. Three of these punts are listed in the “Top-30 NFL Punts of All Time.” And yet, with all these accolades and league-leading accomplishments, Bojorquez has never made a single Pro Bowl. This year seems promising.

item.title: Hollywood Legend LeVar Burton Has Five Special Words For WNBA Champion Gabby Williams
item.description: Nov 4, 2026; San Francisco, California, US; Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams holds the WNBA most valuable player trophy during the Golden State Valkyries championship parade. Mandatory Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images Gabby Williams has not had a quiet week. Since the Golden State Valkyries won the WNBA championship, tributes have rolled in from sports, entertainment, and politics. Michael Jordan sent a text, Stephen Curry cheered the team on, and Barack Obama posted his praise online. Now, a Reading Rainbow legend has joined the list. LeVar Burton congratulated the Finals MVP in a short video that CBS Mornings shared on X. Both were guests on the broadcast. Burton was there to discuss his memoir, Take My Word For It, while Williams was celebrating the Valkyries’ historic run. Burton kept it brief, but the warmth came through. He shook Williams’ hand and delivered his message. “ Congratulations. Really. And I’ve got to say, you are carrying this like a queen. You really are ,” Burton said. “ Congratulations. Many more years of success, or as many as you would like to have. ” SPECIAL MOMENT: Legendary actor and “Reading Rainbow” host @levarburton congratulated Golden State @valkyries star Gabby Williams on her WNBA championship win. Williams was named the 2026 @WNBA Finals MVP after helping lead the Valkyries to their first championship in franchise history. — CBS Mornings (@CBSMornings) November 9, 2026 Burton then introduced his wife, Stephanie, who congratulated Williams as well. Williams answered with a simple thank-you. “ We’re going to come see you next season ,” Burton said. Burton has plenty to cheer. Golden State beat the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 on Oct. 31 at Chase Center. The Valkyries won the title in their second season, a feat described as the fastest by an expansion franchise in major American pro sports. Williams made it happen the hard way. She had 2 points at halftime, and Golden State trailed 30-24. She then scored 28 in the second half, a WNBA postseason record for a single half. She finished with 30. Williams said the break did not rattle her. Coach Natalie Nakase delivered a fiery message, but Williams saw a six-point gap and believed that if she got going, her team would be fine. She was right. Atlanta tied it in the fourth quarter, and Williams answered with a deep three with 2:18 left to make it 60-57. The Valkyries never trailed again. What The Title Means For Gabby Williams After 8 Seasons Of Waiting This was Williams’ eighth WNBA season and her first in Golden State, following three in Chicago and four in Seattle. The wait stretched beyond the league, too. France lost the 2024 Olympic gold medal game to the United States by one point, then lost to the Americans again in the FIBA Women’s World Cup final in September. Williams also won the EuroLeague title with Fenerbahçe in April. Even so, the WNBA trophy was the one she wanted most. The Finals MVP averaged 19.6 points and 2.6 steals in the series.

Burton says he will be there.

item.title: NHL Predictions: Ottawa Senators vs Washington Capitals – November 10
item.description: Apr 7, 2024; Washington, District of Columbia, USA; Washington Capitals right wing Tom Wilson (43) and Capitals center Dylan Strome (17) get into a scrum with Ottawa Senators center Mark Kastelic (12) and Senators left wing Brady Tkachuk (7) at the… | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Levi Pike, Editor Welcome to the battle of the two nations’ iconic capital cities, the Ottawa Senators hosting the team that over the past decade or so, has been involved in many important games, the Washington Capitals, with NHL Predictions alongside us here at Last Word On Hockey . This has turned into a fast-paced, hard-hitting rivalry as head coaches Spencer Carbury and Travis Green enforce physical and defence-oriented systems. So, just who will prevail? And who, will be sensational? Head-to-Head History and Game Details This is the first of three meetings between the two teams, as they play at a spread out frequency through 2026-27, once in January, and once again in April. The last time the two teams met, Thomas Chabot played over 28 minutes in a 4-1 defeat at the hands of the Caps. Linus Ullmark was outclassed by Logan Thompson to earn the two points. However, the Sens did win an earlier season matchup 7-1, and they won the other game for good measure. In any case, these are two evenly matched opponents. This is a standard start time of 7:00 p.m. Eastern, live from the Canadian Tire Centre, in Kanata, Ontario, just outside Ottawa. How to Watch Senators vs Capitals US TV: MNMT, ESPN+ || Canada TV: RDS2, TSN5, Sportsnet+, and of course, available wherever you are on the NHL Center Ice Package. That could only mean one thing, that star netminder Linus Ullmark would be ready to take to the crease in Tuesday’s night matchup with the Caps. As of publication, he is listed as the expected starter for the Sens. Furthermore, Ullmark has been basically lights out for the Sens. This has turned into a fast-paced, hard-hitting rivalry as head coaches Spencer Carbury and Travis Green enforce physical and defence-oriented systems. So, just who will prevail? And who, will be sensational? Head-to-Head History and Game Details This is the first of three meetings between the two teams, as they play at a spread out frequency through 2026-27, once in January, and once again in April. The last time the two teams met, Thomas Chabot played over 28 minutes in a 4-1 defeat at the hands of the Caps. Linus Ullmark was outclassed by Logan Thompson to earn the two points. However, the Sens did win an earlier season matchup 7-1, and they won the other game for good measure. In any case, these are two evenly matched opponents. This is a standard start time of 7:00 p.m. Eastern, live from the Canadian Tire Centre, in Kanata, Ontario, just outside Ottawa. How to Watch Senators vs Capitals US TV: MNMT, ESPN+ || Canada TV: RDS2, TSN5, Sportsnet+, and of course, available wherever you are on the NHL Center Ice Package. April 11, 2025; Ottawa, Ontario, CAN; Ottawa Senators right wing Claude Giroux (28) celebrates a goal scored by centre Dylan Cozens (24) in the first period against the Montreal Canadiens at the Canadian Tire Centre. Mandatory Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn Images Team Form and Key Storylines Ottawa with Another Tough Matchup at Home The big news out of Sens camp, ahead of this game, was that on Sunday the Ottawa Senators assigned goaltender Jonas Johansson back to the AHL’s Belleville Senators . That could only mean one thing, that star netminder Linus Ullmark would be ready to take to the crease in Tuesday’s night matchup with the Caps. As of publication, he is listed as the expected starter for the Sens. Furthermore, Ullmark has been basically lights out for the Sens. He is 7-1-0, with a mesmerizing 1.33 goals-against average, and a .945 save percentage. The other news is that Ridly Greig skated on a line with Michael Amadio and Claude Giroux at practice yesterday. So, we think that means that Greig is ready to go. However, with Greig playing pivot, that means that Shane Pinto has been elevated to play with Drake Batherson. We know that beyond the Tim Stutzle and Drake Batherson stats , and offensive production, the Sens do have solid depth. And that third line, is as solid as it comes. So, the Sens will hope their forward depth can be a differentiator in tonight’s matchup. #Sens lines from practice @ComingInHotSens Zetterlund-Stutzle-Cozens Cousins-Pinto-Batherson Amadio-Greig-Giroux Blais-Halliday-Tomasino Hodgson Sanderson-Zub Chabot-Spence Kleven-Matinpalo Yakemchuk Ullmark Ersson — Alex Adams (@AlexAdamsCIH) November 9, 2026 Capitals Story for NHL Predictions The current Washington Capitals general manager Chris Patrick has done an excellent job of transitioning the organization passed the Alex Ovechkin era. Make no mistake, the era led by the likes of Braden Holtby, Mike Green, Nicklas Backstrom, and Ovi, was a great time in the District of Columbia for hockey fans, young and old. But now the team has been retooled to survive the inevitable, of Ovechkin passing the torch. Among this year’s team leaders for the Caps are high-priced, off-season acquisitions, such as Jordan Kyrou and Alex Tuch. Additionally, Sen fans will remember that it was only a couple of years ago they traded Jakob Chychrun to the Capitals, in exchange for Nick Jensen back in July 2024. Jensen is currently in the Anaheim Ducks organization, and recently cleared waivers, and is making $2.25 million playing for the AHL’s San Diego Gulls. Meanwhile, since Washington acquired Chychrun, he has the 14th-most points among NHL defencemen, with 48 goals and 70 assists, and plays nearly 22-and-a-half minutes a game. One more note for Washington, and although nobody is quite on the pace of Connor McDavid , who entered Tuesday’s play with 28 primary assists, only eight less than the second place person in the scoring race, teammate Leon Draisaitl, has points. But still the fact that Dylan Strome has 11 assists on the campaign, and all of them are primary, is impressive nonetheless. Also, for Sen fans, Tim Stutzle is only one behind that pace with 10 primary assists on the season. Logan Thompson is expected to start for the Caps. His .888 save percentage is sure to improve, as he is a career .910 save percentage level goaltender. NHL Predictions There’s no reason not to expect a tight battle between the two sides. Systematically they play similar, so it’ll be about who’s snipers can lock in their range finder, and really bare down with the opportunities present themself. We like Ottawa, mostly because they are at home, and will be motivated in Ullmark’s return to the lineup. Final Projected Score Projected score: Senators win 3-2 Projected lineups and starting goaltenders are based on available information at the time of writing, and neither team had confirmed its starter. Please check official team sources prior to locking in your daily fantasy lineups. item.title: Four Key Figures From Roma’s 3-0 Win Against Sassuolo
item.description: ROME, ITALY - NOVEMBER 07: Mario Hermoso of AS Roma celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the Serie A match between AS Roma and US Sassuolo at Stadio Olimpico on November 07, 2026 in Rome, Italy. (Photo by Paolo Bruno/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Giallorossi head into the second international break of the season unbeaten after coasting to a 3-0 victory over Sassuolo at the Olimpico on Sunday. The win extends Roma’s unbeaten run in Serie A to 18, dating back to last season. Perhaps the most impressive part has been the injuries the Giallorossi have overcome over the last month to keep that run going. Before the Giallorossi begin to heal their last wounds over the next two weeks, let’s look at some key figures from Saturday’s performance. 3 As in the number of goalkeepers who have now kept a clean sheet for Roma during this Serie A campaign. Yesterday, Devis Vasquez only had to make one save on Nemanja Matic just three minutes into the match to ensure that Roma would blank Sassuolo. However, the fact that Roma has had to play three different goalkeepers and has been able to sustain a defensive record that concedes less than a goal per match and has kept six clean sheets in 11 matches is as much a testament to the outfield players and Gasperini’s system as it is tothe keepers. 31 – Squadre che hanno segnato più di 30 gol dopo 11 partite stagionali di Serie A negli ultimi 65 anni: 33 – Juventus – 2017/18 32 – Napoli – 2017/18 31 – Lazio – 2017/18 31 – #Roma – 2026/27 🆕 Devastante. #RomaSassuolo #SerieA pic.twitter.com/GpZoW0MuZh — OptaPaolo (@OptaPaolo) November 7, 2026 31 As in the number of league goals Roma has scored this season in 11 Serie A matches. That makes Roma just the 4th team in the last 65 years to score 30 or more goals in 11 matches. In fact, Roma has scored 2 or more goals in ten of those matches. The only match the Giallorossi didn’t score in was a 0-0 draw at Como, when they were down a man. And only Barcelona have scored more across Europe’s top 5 leagues (45 and still to play today). Gasperini’s ball has been taken to the next level this season, as management has recruited players who fit his system. Mora’s goal yesterday was his third consecutive league match with a goal after he previously netted against Cagliari and Udinese. He also assisted Matías Soulé‘s opening goal against Manchester United. The young Portuguese talent is finding his feet in Rome and looks like an excellent signing. item.title: Valentino Rossi in new autobiography: '2015 still hurts, Marc Marquez wanted me to lose'
item.description: Motorsport photo Valentino Rossi has revisited his 2015 feud with Marc Marquez in his new autobiography, maintaining that the Spaniard interfered in his MotoGP title battle with Jorge Lorenzo . The nine-time world champion previously published a book about his career while he was still at the peak of his powers. But a new work, La Mia Storia , will be released on 10 November, offering a fresh account of the defining moments of a legendary and often controversial career. Although 11 years have passed, the events of the 2015 Malaysian Grand Prix remain a defining chapter in the Italian's life. Rossi was fighting Lorenzo for what would have been his 10th world title and arrived at Sepang accusing Marquez, with whom he had already been involved in several contentious incidents in Argentina and Assen that year, of conspiring to ensure a Spanish rider won the MotoGP championship. Marquez responded with an uncompromising battle during Sunday's race, which culminated in the infamous clash in which Rossi appeared to kick the Honda rider off his bike. Rossi believed Marquez, who was already out of title contention, was solely intent on losing him the championship. Rossi was subsequently penalised with a back-of-the-grid start in the Valencia finale, where tensions reached unprecedented levels between the three protagonists and among the fans who had travelled to the circuit. The race attracted record television audiences worldwide and ended with Lorenzo being crowned champion, while Rossi accused Marquez of a 'biscotto' – an alleged agreement to avoid attacking Lorenzo and prevent the title from going to the Italian. Rossi appeared on RAI's Che tempo che fa programme on Sunday to promote his new autobiography, which looks back on his sporting career. Inevitably, the interviewer asked him about the events of 2015. Some are lower, some are higher. But the 2015 story makes me even angrier because Marquez wasn't actually fighting for the championship. item.content:encoded: Motorsport photo Valentino Rossi has revisited his 2015 feud with Marc Marquez in his new autobiography, maintaining that the Spaniard interfered in his MotoGP title battle with Jorge Lorenzo . The nine-time world champion previously published a book about his career while he was still at the peak of his powers. But a new work, La Mia Storia , will be released on 10 November, offering a fresh account of the defining moments of a legendary and often controversial career. Although 11 years have passed, the events of the 2015 Malaysian Grand Prix remain a defining chapter in the Italian's life. Rossi was fighting Lorenzo for what would have been his 10th world title and arrived at Sepang accusing Marquez, with whom he had already been involved in several contentious incidents in Argentina and Assen that year, of conspiring to ensure a Spanish rider won the MotoGP championship. Marquez responded with an uncompromising battle during Sunday's race, which culminated in the infamous clash in which Rossi appeared to kick the Honda rider off his bike. Rossi believed Marquez, who was already out of title contention, was solely intent on losing him the championship. Rossi was subsequently penalised with a back-of-the-grid start in the Valencia finale, where tensions reached unprecedented levels between the three protagonists and among the fans who had travelled to the circuit. The race attracted record television audiences worldwide and ended with Lorenzo being crowned champion, while Rossi accused Marquez of a 'biscotto' – an alleged agreement to avoid attacking Lorenzo and prevent the title from going to the Italian. Rossi appeared on RAI's Che tempo che fa programme on Sunday to promote his new autobiography, which looks back on his sporting career. Inevitably, the interviewer asked him about the events of 2015. Rossi insisted that his version of events had not changed, admitting that what happened still hurts and that he regrets how much attention is devoted to the title he lost rather than the championships he won. Valentino Rossi, Yamaha Factory Racing, Marc Márquez, Repsol Honda Team Valentino Rossi, Yamaha Factory Racing, Marc Márquez, Repsol Honda Team “We all have our limits. Some are lower, some are higher. But the 2015 story makes me even angrier because Marquez wasn't actually fighting for the championship. Lorenzo and I were fighting for it; he was only fighting to make me lose. And in the end, he succeeded,” Rossi said. “That is something that never goes away; it still hurts. More than 10 years have passed, but my feelings, my state of mind when I think about it, are still the same as they were on that night in Valencia. And that worries me a little,” he chuckled. “I often look at myself in the mirror and tell myself: let's not focus on the title we lost, let's think about the ones we won. But that's sport; losing hurts more.” Rossi assesses Bezzecchi and Bagnaia Moving on from the past, Rossi also discussed the present, offering his assessment of the performances of his riders in MotoGP through the VR46 Riders Academy, who have endured a challenging season. Marco Bezzecchi , in particular, looked a strong contender early in the campaign, at one stage building a 102-point advantage over Marquez. However, after a series of mistakes despite the competitiveness of his Aprilia, he is now third in the standings behind Jorge Martin with two rounds remaining and on the verge of missing out on the title. “Bezzecchi is doing well because he won [Sunday's Qatar Grand Prix], but he is a little disappointed because he had the opportunity to win the world championship this year. He had the speed, but he made too many mistakes. Most likely, he won't win it,” Rossi said. Read Also: Massimo Rivola: 'Aprilia didn’t lose the championship, Marc Marquez won it' Rossi also commented on Francesco Bagnaia , who is counting down the days until his departure from Ducati after two difficult seasons. His hopes of a strong result in Qatar were dashed when he suffered a foot injury in a crash during Saturday's sprint. “When you break a foot and have two fractures, as is the case with him, you're obviously not in a good way. But considering how the crash happened [a heavy fall following contact with Fermin Aldeguer ], it could have been much worse,” he said. Finally, Rossi discussed the performance of another friend of his academy, Andrea Kimi Antonelli, who has recently been crowned Formula 1 world champion. “Kimi? Spectacular. Having an Italian driver who, after 70 years, makes us so fortunate with a world title is exciting," he said. “There are many Italian riders in the Motorcycle world championship, but not in F1. I've always tried to understand why. Kimi came here because of us, the fans. I've known him for a few years; he's a fantastic person, very funny. He's a champion." Read Also: A water park, “not a rock star” and Toto Wolff’s words – Is Kimi Antonelli really a different F1 champion? To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: Caitlin Clark Reveals Why She Refused To Wear Colts Jersey Despite Backlash
item.description: Oct 5, 2025; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Caitlin Clark looks on from the sideline during warmups before the game between the Las Vegas Raiders and the Indianapolis Colts at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Indiana Fever superstar Caitlin Clark explained on Kylie Kelce’s Not Gonna Lie podcast why she didn’t wear the Indianapolis Colts jersey she received at Lucas Oil Stadium, reaffirming her lifelong loyalty to the Kansas City Chiefs. Last year, Clark and her Fever teammates were honored as special guests at Lucas Oil Stadium for the Colts’ Week Five game against the Las Vegas Raiders. She chose not to wear the Colts jersey the team gifted her, explaining to Kylie , “I have to be loyal to the red, OK?” Answering Kylie’s question about whether she noticed backlash over not wearing the custom Colts jersey, Clark said, “Honestly, in real time, I wasn’t thinking I’m not gonna put this on because I don’t want, like, the Chiefs fans mad or Travis mad or whatever, but after the fact, I didn’t realize that all my teammates had it on, so that made me look worse.” Speaking to Clark about her being spotted at a Colts game without her jersey, it “really struck a chord” for Kylie, who said she has “caught a lot of s*** for not putting the red on” when attending Chiefs games at Arrowhead Stadium with her husband, Jason Kelce. The Fever guard assured the host and her listeners that she still has the custom Colts jersey. Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever pulled up to Colts-Raiders today 🤩 (via @Colts) — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) October 5, 2025 Reaffirming her lifelong Chiefs fandom, Clark added, “But no, I mean, I wish them the best — the Colts. But I am (a) die-hard Chiefs (fan). I’ve been die-hard since I was a young kid. And it is what it is, OK?” Clark, who grew up in Iowa two and a half hours from Arrowhead Stadium, said she supports both teams but remains a die-hard Chiefs fan, even watching their Week Two matchup on television rather than attending. She said it was tough when the Chiefs and Colts played each other in Week Two this year. Explaining why she watched the Chiefs-Colts game on TV, Clark said, “I can’t wear Chief stuff, but be in Indianapolis. So it was in KC; I didn’t go to it. But I was watching (it) on TV.” Clark grew up in Iowa in a family of Chiefs fans. Reflecting on her childhood Chiefs fandom, Clark said, “There’s (sic) pictures of me as a young kid in a full pink Chiefs fit, bob cut, (…) (I was) raised in it.” Describing childhood trips to Chiefs games growing up in West Des Moines, Iowa, Clark recalled, “I mean, I grew up two and a half hours from the stadium. So it was always a once-a-year trip. I went with my cousins. We were probably in the nosebleeds. item.title: 2027: Nnaji vows to end excessive taxation in Enugu
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has said he is contesting the 2027 election to rescue the state from what he described as excessive taxation and its impact on businesses and residents. Nnaji alleged that the high tax burden was forcing businessmen and investors to relocate from the state, adding that Enugu had become one of the most expensive places to do business in the country. He spoke while addressing indigenes of Enugu State resident in Aba, Abia State, under the umbrella of the Enugu State Consultative Forum, Abia State chapter. The former Minister of Science and Technology pledged to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, job creation and measures to address insecurity and unemployment. He said he had been consulting Enugu indigenes living outside the state to draw their attention to what he described as the challenges facing the state and seek their support ahead of the election. Nnaji expressed concern over what he described as the return of armed robbery in parts of Enugu, attributing the development to unemployment, hunger and economic hardship. He promised to establish industries that would create employment opportunities, reduce poverty and take more than 50,000 youths off the streets. “What is happening in Enugu State is condemnable. Enugu is for all, but today, businessmen and investors are relocating from the state due to excessive taxation. And the state government doesn’t care. “Our people are suffering from excessive taxation, even in the rural areas. Traders in rural communities only open their businesses in the evening when tax officials have left. Government collects N36,000 from traders in the villages, when most of them do not make such an amount annually. “Tax is based on profit, not on shops, as they are doing in Enugu. People are hungry. Armed people now invade homes at midnight to collect phones, computers and food items such as rice, beans and garri. This is something that happened more than 20 years ago,” he said. He promised to establish industries that would create employment opportunities, reduce poverty and take more than 50,000 youths off the streets. “What is happening in Enugu State is condemnable. Enugu is for all, but today, businessmen and investors are relocating from the state due to excessive taxation. And the state government doesn’t care. “Our people are suffering from excessive taxation, even in the rural areas. Traders in rural communities only open their businesses in the evening when tax officials have left. Government collects N36,000 from traders in the villages, when most of them do not make such an amount annually. “Tax is based on profit, not on shops, as they are doing in Enugu. People are hungry. Armed people now invade homes at midnight to collect phones, computers and food items such as rice, beans and garri. This is something that happened more than 20 years ago,” he said. The PDP candidate also questioned the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), claiming that it had risen from N26 billion to N406.7 billion. He compared the figure with the revenue generated by Abia and Anambra states, arguing that the high revenue collection raised questions about the state’s taxation policies and their impact on businesses. Nnaji further alleged that Enugu’s debt profile had increased significantly under the current administration, although he did not provide figures to substantiate the claim. He said government should focus on creating wealth and improving the living conditions of residents rather than imposing taxes that could undermine businesses. “We have set up the Enugu State Recovery Committee, with me as chairman. This is why we are visiting Enugu people residing outside the state, telling them about the poor situation of things in their state. “Last week, we were at Alaba International Market, and we have visited many places. I want to recover Enugu. Once we win, we will build industries based on coal, iron ore and cement. There will be no more excessive taxation in Enugu when I win,” he said. He also expressed concern over the condition of roads in Isi-Uzo Local Government Area, questioning how the state government had utilised its internally generated revenue and monthly federal allocations. In their separate remarks, the Director-General of the Uche Nnaji Campaign Organisation, Chuks Ndukwe, and Chief Uche Ugwu said the PDP candidate’s campaign was focused on industrialisation, employment generation and economic recovery. They criticised the state’s taxation policies, arguing that they had placed pressure on businesses and traders. The campaign officials also expressed confidence in the PDP’s grassroots support, describing Enugu as a traditional stronghold of the party. PDP senatorial candidates, including Nweke Kingsley Chizoba (Enugu East) and Nestor Ezeme (Enugu North), urged Nnaji to remain committed to his ambition, expressing confidence in his support among residents. Earlier, the President of the Enugu State Consultative Forum, Hon. Sunday Okonkwo, said Nnaji’s manifesto addressed issues affecting the state, including industrialisation, security and youth empowerment. He said the forum was interested in governance proposals that would address the challenges confronting businesses and residents of Enugu State. item.title: ‘Without storyboards, I feel like I’m in Grand Central station in my underwear’: film’s fightback against AI
item.description: As Hollywood begins to adopt the technology, the professionals in most direct jeopardy are the illustrators mapping out directors’ first visions. They sketch out what could be lost A film industry dominated by AI is a dystopian prospect: stories and dialogue generated by large language models, populated by reincarnated screen icons and uncanny humanoids . That is in the future, but the real-world impact of AI is already directly affecting jobs behind the scenes, as Hollywood’s biggest film-makers begin to adopt the technology. James Cameron – long an advocate for emerging technologies in film-making – is on the board of a gen AI firm , citing his interest in how AI will intersect with CGI; Steven Soderbergh used Meta-powered tech to create animations for his recent documentary about John Lennon ; even Christopher Nolan, while dismissing the idea that AI will replace humans as “nonsense”, conceded that it will create some useful “imaging tools”. The current canary in the coalmine however is the storyboard artist, whose work gen AI appears to have directly in its sights. Storyboard artists are the illustrators who draw the panels of images with notes and diagrams that map out scenes before they are filmed. Storyboards are used to work out how a film will look, and as a blueprint to communicate a director’s vision to cast and crew , and are one of the first steps in bringing a script off the page. Now they appear on the verge of replacement by programmes that use text prompts to create illustrations instead. Even an old-school diehard like Martin Scorsese has got on board; in June he announced a partnership with an AI firm whose text-to-image model he used in the storyboarding process for his next movie. Continue reading...

item.title: 'Avatar' Officially Unveils a Very Different Version of Zuko in New Book
item.description: 2026 has been a fantastic year to be a fan of the Avatar franchise — the elemental fantasy saga, not the blue alien sci-fi movies. The animated sequel series Avatar: Seven Havens has been phenomenally successful, with a second season already confirmed, and Paramount Studios even has an Avatar fighting game that actually feels great to play. However, arguably the biggest win for Avatar fans this year was Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender . Set 12 years after Avatar: The Last Airbender ended, the movie reunited the gang for a new adventure. And even though it didn't get a theatrical release as originally promised, it was still a win for Team Avatar.

item.title: Ransomware threat blares from Vanderbilt University computers during cyberattack
item.description: Classes at Vanderbilt University are proceeding as scheduled today, although access to most university systems remains restricted following a cyberattack claimed by ransomware group BYOD. Vanderbilt announced on Monday morning that it was dealing with "an active cybersecurity incident," and that the fallout may affect university devices, systems, and cloud-based services. The Nashville-based university initially told students and staff to shut down university devices and disconnect from campus Wi-Fi. It warned them to watch for unexpected prompts, altered files or permissions, unfamiliar applications, and unsolicited authentication requests. Campus computers reportedly began playing an audio threat attributed to BYOD. Student newspaper The Vanderbilt Hustler cited posts on campus social network Fizz showing the message. "You have been compromised by BYOD," the recording said. "We suggest you reach out to us as soon as possible. Instructions have been placed on your desktop. Failure to communicate will result in this estate being brought to the ground completely. Make the right choice or rot with the wrong one." By Monday evening, Vanderbilt had restored access to campus Wi-Fi, but warned that access to most systems remains restricted. "We know this has disrupted important work and caused frustration across the university," it said . "Vanderbilt Information Technology is working with government agencies and other partners to manage this situation." Students were told to attend classes as scheduled on Tuesday and contact instructors about flexibility on coursework deadlines. Staff were instructed to report to work normally. Vanderbilt's Athletics department said that its ticketing system was unavailable, and that students were unable to claim tickets for the college's football game against Alabama on Saturday. BYOD claimed responsibility for the attack on Vanderbilt on Monday, along with extensive data theft. "If you could not tell already, your databases are locked [and] we have your entire estate and research data," it said via its leak site. "Over 1 million SSNs, full names, email addresses, phone numbers, student and employee records, full takeover of your DC, whatever was on your network, we possess." Vanderbilt has not confirmed BYOD's claims about the extent of its access or the data allegedly stolen. BYOD may be a familiar name to some. The group previously claimed attacks on the University of New Mexico and Trump Mobile's customer database . BYOD also claimed responsibility on Monday for an attack on Texas Health and Human Services. The agency has not publicly confirmed an incident and did not immediately respond to our questions. ®
